purpose: Perform one read-only, grant-bound Identity lookup for an authorized Support operator and return the minimum approved Account context.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-173 adds the private DEV/TEST operator browser workflow around the existing Identity lookup. The owning interface, grant lifecycle and standard Audit selection are preserved. The review correction clears form values and diagnostics on pagehide and navigate-replaces persisted restorations with an authorized GET. WELL-174 wraps private parsing and dispatch so response scrubbing covers parser failures and removes Set-Cookie from returned telemetry metadata. WELL-189 refreshes shared source references. The mapped behavior is unchanged. WELL-210 refreshes the shared browser proof source reference after the Recovery packet path moved to v0.3.0. The mapped behavior is unchanged.

collaborating_domains.interface: No runtime Audit write for this ordinary low-risk lookup; the selected Audit contract classifies it as E3 normally.
collaborating_domains.ownership: Audit evidence does not authorize the lookup. Identity retains Account and Support-grant authority; the ordinary low-risk lookup does not create a second central Audit record.

ash.caller_boundary: Private Identity authority. The lookup action locks and revalidates the named Support grant; no resource action exposes an Account directory.
Identity reads only the grant-bound Account inside the owner's transaction and returns a four-field projection.

arguments: Current Identity Session credentials, IdentityGrant id, grant-bound Account id and an email to canonicalize and compare.
returns: {:ok, %{account_id, account_status, email_verified?, security_posture}} for an authorized match.
{:error, :support_lookup_unavailable} for denied, malformed or unavailable authority.
side_effects: Read-only Identity transaction; no Account mutation, recovery completion, email change, grant expansion or durable lookup record.
caller_constraints: The caller needs a current named Support grant scoped to identity_lookup, reason-coded security_review and the exact Account, a current eligible Session, active MFA and a current lookup_identity step-up.
The authorized caller may distinguish a match from a non-match only for this grant-bound target; the function is not a public endpoint or directory.

arguments: Credentials, grant id, target Account id and submitted email.
returns: The public Identity result described by lookup_support_identity/4.
side_effects: Locks current actor, target, Session, Token and grant through PrivilegedAccess, then performs an exact target-to-canonical-email comparison.
caller_constraints: All invalid or stale authority paths collapse to support_lookup_unavailable.

request_flow.summary: An internal caller supplies a current Identity Session, one grant and one target; no browser or public controller exposes the lookup result.
Identity locks and rechecks actor, target, Session, bearer Token, grant lifecycle, role, scope, purpose, expiry and assurance before comparing the canonical email.
Only the minimum Account status projection or an authorized :not_found result is returned; all denied paths share one unavailable result.

Sign in through the existing password Session journey, then open /dev/support/account-access in an enabled DEV/TEST build. Submit the known synthetic Support grant, Account ID and email with the operator password and a current authenticator code. The browser passes only this POST intent and current cookie credentials to Identity. A successful lookup presents Account status, email verification and security posture. A fresh GET has no previous result.

guards: The owning Identity grant-revocation action validates its current actor and reason; every lookup rechecks current grant state and expiry.
side_effects: The existing grant lifecycle invalidates elevated Session assurance.

security_invariants.summary: The grant names a Support Account, role, identity_lookup scope, security_review reason, exact target, independent approver, bounded lifetime and active/revoked state; other reason codes and role labels alone do not authorize lookup.
Current Session, bearer Token, eligible actor, active MFA, purpose-bound unexpired step-up, assurance versions, grant lifecycle and exact target are checked inside the Identity transaction.
The projection contains only Account id, Account status, email verification and security posture; it excludes email, names, credential state and recovery detail.
No generic Super Admin bypass, impersonation, account list, correction, recovery completion, email mutation or grant expansion is exposed.

The browser route rejects query strings and requires CSRF for explicit POST. The controller revalidates the current cookie Session and establishes lookup_identity assurance before Identity locks and checks the named current grant. Browser denial collapses no match and rejected authority to one response after authentication. All lookup responses are no-store. The dispatcher clears parsed values and diagnostics before Bandit request-stop telemetry and suppresses SQL payload events for matching synchronous Repo operations.

The same-origin lookup script resets operator inputs and destroys diagnostics on pagehide. On persisted pageshow it clears again and calls location.replace with the fixed form URL. A fresh GET rechecks the current Session without resubmitting lookup intent. A subsequent explicit POST still needs fresh MFA and a current named grant.

concurrency.summary: The owner transaction locks Accounts in deterministic id order, then current Token, Session and grant authority; concurrent grant revocation arbitrates on the same locked grant row.

idempotency_retry.summary: Lookup is read-only. Repeated calls create no new state and each retry revalidates current Session, grant and purpose-bound assurance.

The browser stores no lookup result. A new submission needs a fresh valid authenticator period and repeats the owner checks. Existing durable Account locking and TOTP replay prevention govern competing step-up requests.

failure_recovery.summary: Missing, malformed, wrong-actor, wrong-scope, wrong-reason, expired, revoked, stale-session and stale-assurance authority returns the same support_lookup_unavailable error. Migration rollback refuses while identity_lookup grants remain, preserving those grant rows instead of rewriting their scope.
An authorized non-match returns :not_found without mutation; a later retry still requires fresh current authorization.

cases: Authorized matching and non-matching lookup for the exact grant target.
Duplicate read stability and exact minimum projection.
Missing, wrong-scope, wrong-actor, expired and revoked grant denials.
Non-security-review grant reason and malformed grant, target and email inputs deny generically.
Invalid and revoked Session, wrong-purpose step-up and stale MFA-version assurance denials.
Unrelated target denial and no Super Admin capability bypass.
A permitted control with the same credentials and grant, followed by wrong-target denial and rejection of a separately scoped self grant.
tests.proves: The real Identity interface returns a narrow result only under current named Support authority and otherwise hides account classification behind one generic error.
tests.limits: These tests call the Identity interface directly. The browser integration is exercised separately.

cases: CSRF rejection, current Session, disabled and anonymous entry, query rejection and TOTP replay.
Real Chromium sign-in, keyboard focus, narrow reflow, fresh MFA, minimum projection, fresh request after grant revocation and payload-free request-stop and SQL telemetry.

Native Chromium Back/Forward after sensitive entry, grant revocation and logout. Check real pagehide clearing, persisted-event handling on an actual POST document, authorized blank GET replacement, no additional POST and fresh 404 GETs after logout.
tests.proves: The private synthetic browser workflow reuses the owning Identity checks and does not persist the lookup result.
tests.limits: Chromium uses a loopback TEST endpoint and a deterministic TOTP clock. The fixture revokes the grant separately through its real Ash action. It does not model production staff provisioning or external monitoring. The POST restoration test dispatches persisted events on the actual Chromium document because native admission to the back-forward cache varies by browser. The separate history navigation tests traverse real entries.

safe_extensions.summary: A future approved Support operation requires its own bounded scope, purpose, target restriction, projection and tests through Identity.

reuse.summary: Reuse P8-13 IdentityGrant and current Session/MFA/step-up authorization; the new scope adds no parallel Support or Account authority.
The selected Audit contract classifies ordinary low-risk Support lookup as E3 normally; no central Audit write is needed for this read-only lookup.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not replace the named actor, purpose-bound current Session, scope, target and expiry checks with a role label or Super Admin flag.
Do not expose arbitrary Account search, an unauthenticated endpoint, raw Account/security fields, correction, recovery or email mutation through lookup.

proof_limitations: Proof uses synthetic development/test Accounts and grants. Production grant issuance and operator route activation remain outside the ticket.
Authorized matching and non-matching results differ by design; the denial boundary remains generic and the function is not exposed publicly.
The lookup is read-only and does not create an Audit event; selected Audit authority classifies ordinary low-risk lookup as E3 normally.

The HTTP adapter starts request telemetry before application dispatch and can observe the existing encrypted cookie transport. The browser does not send lookup data in the URL or expose decoded cookie values to request-stop telemetry.
The browser-history mitigation requires the scoped script to run. The server continues to require current authority on every network request.

sources.symbol: two independent Sessions transactions cannot consume one TOTP period twice
